# @zakkster/lite-cellular

> Zero-GC Worley/cellular noise for 2D and 3D. `cellular2(x, y, out?)` returns the two nearest feature-point distances `f1`/`f2` and the F1 owner's cell `id`, written into a caller-owned out-struct -- **no allocation on the query path.** v1.0.0 ships the three distance metrics (euclidean/manhattan/chebyshev, fixed at instance creation) and the module free-function surface; v1.1.0 adds the zero-alloc field baker `fillCellField2` and the EXACTLY-seamless `tileableCell2`; v1.2.0 LIFTS the whole surface into 3D (`cellular3` / `fillCellField3` / `tileableCell3`); v1.3.0 makes the neighbourhood EXACT per metric (chebyshev 3x3/3x3x3, euclid/manhattan 5x5/5x5x5 -- an L1/L2 ball reaches a feature two cells away; decisions/0008). Sibling of `@zakkster/lite-noise` (gradient noise); the two compose at the app layer, never in the same file.

## API

Named exports (v1.3.0): `createCellular`, `Cellular`, `cellular2`, `seedCellular`,
`VERSION`, `METRIC_EUCLIDEAN`, `METRIC_MANHATTAN`, `METRIC_CHEBYSHEV`. The C2 methods
(`fillCellField2`, `tileableCell2`) and the C3 3D methods (`cellular3`,
`fillCellField3`, `tileableCell3`) are INSTANCE methods -- a bake wants metric +
jitter control, which is what an instance is for. No module-surface baker, tileable,
or 3D surface, by design; no 4D (decisions/0007).

```ts
// Distance metric ids. 0 (euclidean, default), 1 (manhattan), 2 (chebyshev).
// Anything else throws at construction -- the guard accepts 0/1/2 and widens the
// set from v0.1.0, it never loosens (fail-closed).
const METRIC_EUCLIDEAN: 0;
const METRIC_MANHATTAN: 1;
const METRIC_CHEBYSHEV: 2;

// Package version, in lockstep with package.json + llms.txt (three-place sync).
const VERSION: string;

interface CellularResult { f1: number; f2: number; id: number; }
interface CellularOptions { metric?: number; jitter?: number; }

class Cellular {
    // Validates metric (0/1/2 else throws) and jitter (finite, [0,1] else throws)
    // ONCE, at construction, and binds ONE metric-specific kernel to this._kernel.
    // Both immutable for the instance's life. Stores scalars plus one reused
    // out-struct -- no permutation table.
    constructor(seed?: number, opts?: CellularOptions);

    // Sample the field. Returns { f1, f2, id }: nearest and second feature-point
    // distances (in this instance's metric, LINEAR units) and the F1 owner's cell
    // id (signed int32, SMI-safe, stable per Voronoi region, metric-dependent
    // owner). Writes into `out` if given (and returns it), else returns the
    // instance's reused out-struct. THROWS on non-finite x or y. Zero allocation
    // either way. `f2 - f1` (cracks) is the caller's one subtraction.
    cellular2(x: number, y: number, out?: CellularResult): CellularResult;

    // EXACTLY-tileable sample: cellular2 with each neighbour's INTEGER cell coord
    // reduced mod the period, so the field is bit-identically periodic (f1/f2/id at
    // x and x+periodX are ===, not merely close on representable coords) and seamless
    // BY CONSTRUCTION -- strictly better than a float-lattice tile's epsilon seam.
    // periodX/periodY are REQUIRED positive integers (0, negatives, non-integers,
    // NaN, Infinity throw -- there is no default). Zero allocation. See decisions/0006.
    tileableCell2(x: number, y: number, periodX: number, periodY: number, out?: CellularResult): CellularResult;

    // Bake a w*h field into a caller-owned typed array (Float64Array/Float32Array,
    // length >= w*h), row-major, allocation-free; returns dst. combo decoded to a
    // small int ONCE before the loop (never a per-pixel string parse); metric bound
    // once (no per-pixel branch); the scan writes one reused scratch struct (no
    // per-pixel object). Fail closed: non-positive-integer w/h, an undersized or
    // non-typed-array dst, and an unknown combo each throw. See decisions/0005.
    //   opts (all optional, guarded so the omitted-opts path allocates nothing):
    //     scale = 0.01            coord step per pixel (px += scale)
    //     combo = 'f1'            'f1' | 'f2-f1' (alias 'cracks') | 'f2'; unknown throws
    //     jitter = <instance>     override the instance jitter for this bake (bounds-validated
                            like the constructor -- outside [0,1] / non-finite throws)
    //     ox, oy = 0              world-space origin
    //     normalize = false       opt-in in-place remap to [0,1] (constant -> all-zero)
    //     periodX, periodY        set BOTH (positive ints) for a seamless tile of that
    //                             many cells (0006 wrap; pick scale = periodX / w);
    //                             omit both for a plain field
    fillCellField2<T extends Float64Array | Float32Array>(dst: T, w: number, h: number, opts?: object): T;

    // --- 3D (v1.2.0): the 3D lift of the three methods above (decisions/0007) ---
    // Sample the 3D field at (x, y, z): chebyshev 3x3x3 = 27 cells, euclid/manhattan
    // 5x5x5 = 125 cells (0008). Same { f1, f2, id } shape plus depth, this instance's metric.
    // same zero-alloc shape. Writes into `out` if given (returns it) else the reused
    // struct. THROWS on non-finite x, y, or z. Instance-only (no module 3D surface).
    cellular3(x: number, y: number, z: number, out?: CellularResult): CellularResult;

    // EXACTLY-tileable 3D sample: cellular3 with each neighbour's INTEGER cell coord
    // reduced mod its period on ALL THREE axes, so the volume is bit-identically
    // periodic and seamless BY CONSTRUCTION. periodX/periodY/periodZ are REQUIRED
    // positive integers (0, negatives, non-integers, NaN, Infinity throw). Zero alloc.
    tileableCell3(x: number, y: number, z: number, periodX: number, periodY: number, periodZ: number, out?: CellularResult): CellularResult;

    // Bake a w*h*d VOLUME into a caller-owned typed array (length >= w*h*d), row-major
    // with z outermost (idx = (z*h + y)*w + x), allocation-free; returns dst. combo
    // decoded once, metric bound once, one reused scratch struct. Fail closed: bad
    // w/h/d, undersized/non-typed-array dst, unknown combo throw. opts as fillCellField2
    // plus oz and periodZ (set ALL THREE periods for a seamless tile).
    fillCellField3<T extends Float64Array | Float32Array>(dst: T, w: number, h: number, d: number, opts?: object): T;

    // Re-seed in place. Setup cost only -- not on any hot path. Returns this.
    reseed(seed: number): this;
}

// Create an independent instance. Throws on a bad metric id or out-of-range jitter.
function createCellular(seed?: number, opts?: CellularOptions): Cellular;

// Module free surface: euclidean, jitter 1, on a shared module seed. The
// zero-config convenience (metric/jitter control require an instance, by design).
function cellular2(x: number, y: number, out?: CellularResult): CellularResult;

// Re-seed the shared module field. Setup only; auto-seeded 0 on load. Warns once
// in dev builds when called more than once (the last caller wins); silent when
// NODE_ENV==='production'. For independent fields, give each its own createCellular.
function seedCellular(seed?: number): void;
```

## Metrics and jitter

The three metrics share ONE feature-point placement and differ only in the
distance line: euclidean `sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)` (squared in the loop, two sqrts off
it), manhattan `|dx|+|dy|`, chebyshev `max(|dx|,|dy|)` -- all in LINEAR units, so
`cheby.f <= euclid.f <= manhattan.f` holds pointwise for f1 and f2, and `f2 - f1`
stays usable as a mask/displacement. The metric is dropped from the hot loop and
bound once as `this._kernel`, so the neighbourhood scan is monomorphic and branch-free.

Each grid cell scatters one feature point at `cell + 0.5 + jitter*(u-0.5)` where
`u`/`v` in `[0,1)` come from a hash of the integer cell coords + seed. `jitter` in
`[0,1]`: `0` is the exact grid of cell centres, `1` is full Worley. The bound is a
correctness precondition -- `jitter <= 1` keeps every feature point inside its cell,
which is what makes the neighbourhood scan guaranteed to contain the true `f1`/`f2` at
each metric's EXACT radius (0008): chebyshev is exact in the 3x3 / 3x3x3 neighbourhood,
but an L1/L2 unit-cell ball can reach a feature two cells away, so euclidean and
manhattan scan the 5x5 / 5x5x5 neighbourhood. The tileable exact-`===` periodicity
(0006) is unchanged.

Isolation (NS-01): two `createCellular` instances never cross-contaminate, and
`seedCellular` never perturbs an instance -- an instance owns its seed, the module
surface owns the shared one.

## Field bake and tileability

`fillCellField2(dst, w, h, opts)` is the money surface: a whole `w*h` field baked
into a caller-owned typed array with ZERO allocation (`combo` resolved once, metric
bound once, one reused scratch struct -- no per-pixel object, no per-pixel string
parse). `combo` picks the texture: `'f1'` blobs, `'f2-f1'` cracks (alias `'cracks'`),
`'f2'` soft cells. `normalize: true` remaps to `[0,1]` in place (a constant field maps
to all-zero, never NaN).

`tileableCell2` and a tiling bake wrap the INTEGER cell coordinate mod an integer
period, so the tile is seamless BY CONSTRUCTION: because the reduction is integer
modulo (no float period, no grid-alignment precondition), the wrapped cells are the
SAME cells with the SAME feature points, and the seam step equals a normal interior
step. `@zakkster/lite-patternforge` `seamlessScore` reads genuinely near-zero on a
256x256 period-4 cellular tile (~0.012, imperceptible) -- materially below a
`@zakkster/lite-noise` `tileableField2` gradient tile scored the same way (~0.024),
whose lattice wrap carries a small seam-contrast floor. For a seamless bake set
`periodX`/`periodY` and `scale = periodX / w` so the `w` columns span exactly the tile.

## 3D (v1.2.0)

`cellular3` / `tileableCell3` / `fillCellField3` lift the whole surface into 3D over
the per-metric neighbourhood (chebyshev 3x3x3 = 27 cells, euclid/manhattan 5x5x5 = 125
cells; 0008) -- a verbatim lift of the 2D decisions with the coordinate count bumped
2 -> 3 (decisions/0007). Same `{ f1, f2, id }` shape plus
depth, same three metrics bound once (`cheby <= euclid <= manhattan` holds in R^3 for
f1 and f2), same jitter/id/combo rules, and the same EXACT integer-cell tile wrap now
on all three axes. The feature point of a 3D cell scatters via three decorrelated hash
draws (u, v, w). Cost is ~3x the 2D per-query work by cell count (27/9); `cellular3`
euclidean ~4.8 Mops/s against the 2D ~14.3, with `bytesPerCall: 0` on every 3D surface
(proven by torture T6, incl. `maxArrayBuffersGrowth: 0` and a `dst.buffer.byteLength`
assert on the volume bake). The 2D surface is byte-unchanged (all three 2D goldens
re-derive). Instance-only: no module 3D surface, and no 4D ever (out of scope
permanently). `fillCellField3` writes the volume row-major with z outermost
(`idx = (z*h + y)*w + x`); the volumetric use cases are 3D caustics, voxel terrain
masks, animated 2D-over-time (a slab per frame), and marble solids.

```js
import { createCellular } from '@zakkster/lite-cellular';
const cell = createCellular(42);
const r = cell.cellular3(3.5, 7.25, 1.5);   // { f1, f2, id }, zero-alloc
const vol = new Float64Array(32 * 32 * 32);
cell.fillCellField3(vol, 32, 32, 32, { combo: 'f2-f1', scale: 0.05 });
```

## Install

```bash
npm i @zakkster/lite-cellular
```

```js
import { createCellular, METRIC_MANHATTAN } from '@zakkster/lite-cellular';
const cell = createCellular(42, { metric: METRIC_MANHATTAN });
const c = cell.cellular2(3.5, 7.25);   // { f1, f2, id }
const cracks = c.f2 - c.f1;            // Voronoi edges, caller-side
```

## When not to use

- Full Voronoi topology (edges, vertices, adjacency, Lloyd relaxation) -- a geometry
  structure, a different library. This is the noise field, not the diagram.
- Gradient/Simplex/Perlin noise -- that is `@zakkster/lite-noise`. No overlap.
- Curl/flow off cellular -- `f1` has derivative discontinuities at cell boundaries
  by construction, so it cannot feed an analytic flow field. Use lite-noise for flow.
- Cryptographic seeding -- the hash is for reproducible scatter, not security.
- World-scale beyond ~2^52 -- past the float64 integer limit the neighbourhood
  degenerates (the pinned v1.0.0 limit; coords up to 1e12 stay fully precise).
